## What landed (engineering deliverables)

### 1. The Wave-C gate + plan (`ops/src/ops/wave_c.py`, new)

`sig.wave-c-gate/1` — judges **recorded** inputs, never the
wall clock, and emits `go`/`no-go` per leg; exit `0`/`42`/`2`
via `sig-ops wave-c-gate --inputs <json>` (a no-go names the
verbatim re-run prompt). `sig.wave-c-plan/1` — the
deterministic receipted step list via `sig-ops wave-c-plan
[--json]` (19 steps).

Legs L1→L5 in order — a leg admits only when every earlier
leg is recorded green or held-reported (a missed leg is
reported, never silently skipped, OM-19). Criteria, each
refuse-on-fail:

- **`go`** — the ING-GO-C verbatim byte-exact + a parseable
  `recorded_at` (silence is never consent; a paraphrase is a
  refusal).
- **`window`** — the supplied `now` inside 2026-11-16 →
  11-20; the earliest 10-26 start only when all of P37.1,
  PKG-07, Q-23 are recorded landed (`early_landings`);
  L4's read-only soak may also read inside the 48 h grace;
  AR-3's 03:00–06:30Z never-band binds the mutation legs.
- **`q23`** — the adopted answer recorded (cap 40 GB,
  pre-grow 25 GB, temporary tier bump).
- **`review`** — `osm_overpass`'s review-status read green.
  **Read, never written** — this row flips nothing (HG-03 is
  the operator's act; SIG-INGEST-036).
- **`order`/`scope`** — `completed` covers the prefix; leg
  days non-decreasing; `run_set` == `["osm_overpass"]` on L3,
  empty elsewhere (the mirror targets are never a run
  input — their retirement rides the committed registry
  diff).
- **`exclusions`/`serialize`** — no materialize/G2/cut-day
  active; one manual run at a time across waves (P36.12's
  sequencing rule).
- **`wave_b_pause`** (FEA-15) — all four early-fire r11
  batch rows (`r11-layers-01`, `r11-layers-02`,
  `r11-ate-01`, `r11-procurement-01` — the dom-16…19 crons
  inside the window) recorded held before L3's run.
- **`prestate`/`backup`** (L1) — the OM-14 capture + the
  AR-2 `SUCCESSFUL` read-back before the first mutation.
- **`tier_go`** (L2) — the in-ticket pause: a recorded
  verbatim go that is *not* the ING-GO-C text (the wave's go
  is never the tier's); missing or borrowed → refusal.
- **`soak_ready`** (L4) — ≥24 h measured from the recorded
  run end.
- **Close-phase evidence** — `disk` (≥25 GB, limit 40,
  recorded), `tier` (read-backs `db-custom-2-7680` up /
  `db-custom-1-3840` down), `rebuild` (one `sha256:` digest
  across both jobs + `declared_published`), `retarget`
  (`12 8 24 * *`), `run` (ok + `claims_added` > 0), `tiles`
  (±2 % of discovery, ≤ 154,814 taginfo), `privacy`
  (`user_uid_captures == 0`), `plus0` (`claims_added == 0`),
  `er` (`merge_pct ≥ 95.0` of the 132,689 republish rows,
  measured integer `net_new`, `lineage_recorded` —
  republish↔origin one lineage, never independent
  corroboration), `retire` (exactly the two named mirrors;
  the four CCTV targets still scheduled; `derived_from`
  recorded; non-empty `next_fire` after the retirement),
  `soak` (the read + instance_ok + no-materialize-overlap +
  record_ref), `revert` (post-state recorded).

### 2. The driver (`ops/gcp/wave-c.sh`, new)

- `--check` — plan-only print (the step list + the
  recorded-inputs template); no ADC, no network, exit `0`.
- `--apply --leg L1…L5 --inputs <json>` — requires
  `SIG_GCP_PROJECT` + usable gcloud ADC (exit 3 absent —
  refuses rather than fabricating), invokes the gate first
  (a no-go exits 42 before any production command), then
  runs the leg's steps in the restore-point order: OM-14
  pre-state → AR-2 backup polled DONE → `SUCCESSFUL` → disk
  pre-grow (one-way — a resumed run reads state, never
  re-grows) → the tier bump only under the recorded verbatim
  go → the jobs reconciled on one pinned digest +
  declaration bundle republished → the retarget read-back →
  the manual national run → the §7.7 verify set → the `+0`
  re-run → the ER rematerialize → the retirement record →
  the soak → the revert. No source permission flips
  anywhere; missed/held legs are reported, never skipped.

### 3. The `paused_until` due-set bound (FEA-15)

- `ops/src/ops/scheduled.py` — `BatchCadence.paused_until`
  parsed from the row (ISO date string).
- `ops/src/ops/dispatcher.py` — `evaluate_due` skips a
  covering bound even when `state` flips to `"enabled"`
  (`declared-paused-until`); a malformed bound is a
  `DispatcherError` (fails closed); an expired bound is
  inert record, never cleaned up (removal-with-record).
- `ops/src/ops/live_diff.py` — the declared fleet's
  `DeclaredTrigger.paused` posture honours the bound
  (UTC date compare).
- `ops/gcp/scheduled-ops.sh` — `read_batch_rows` carries the
  field; the dispatch-job candidate list and the per-batch
  reconcile hold the trigger PAUSED while the bound covers
  today; the bound never *enables* anything (the row's own
  wave resume does).

`osm_surveillance_deflock` + `osm_surveillance_alpr_nationwide`

restore record ("re-add under `[[targets]]` with

expands exactly the kept set.
